decision_reason: CSI Piemonte's repository identifies MACHI as a city-facing Digital City Platform and the public consortium is its credited developer, but the assigned repo is an umbrella description whose essential front-end and back-end-for-frontend code is in separate public repositories without an inspected grant. The repository is quiet since 2021, and no current primary deployment/use evidence for MACHI was found. Hold pending proof of complete family licensing and current product use/source correspondence.

government_provenance.note: The first-party project README credits CSI Piemonte and defines this specific MACHI platform. CSI's official governance page describes the public member entities and regional public-administration role of the consortium: https://www.csipiemonte.it/it/chi-siamo/azienda/governance. This is CSI product authorship, not inferred from the Developers Italia listing.

public_source.note: The CSI repository is public and points to the two implementation repositories, machife and machibff, which are also publicly accessible. The assigned repository is the canonical MACHI project/architecture record, but it does not contain the complete application implementation.

eligible_license.note: The assigned repository README declares EUPL-1.2-or-later and its root LICENSE.txt is EUPL v1.2 for source published in that repo. The README identifies separate essential implementation repositories https://github.com/csipiemonte/machife and https://github.com/csipiemonte/machibff; neither repository has a root LICENSE file or an explicit license statement in its README. CSI's root grant is not assumed to cover these separate repositories, so the full product license scope is unresolved.

primary_evidence.note: The source describes the intended city portal, authenticated services, notifications, and personal-data dashboard, but I found no current CSI or municipal primary page documenting an operational MACHI deployment or current use. The repository has no published releases and its last push was 2021; a Developers Italia record is only a discovery/metadata lead.

product_identity: MACHI Digital City Platform: an authenticated city portal/web app integrating municipal data, citizen services, insights, preferences, and notifications
agency: CSI Piemonte, a regional public-member ICT consortium/in-house provider for public administrations
geography: Piedmont, Italy; the repo describes a city platform, but no specific current municipal deployment was verified
license: EUPL-1.2-or-later is declared for source in the assigned umbrella repository; license scope for the separate machife and machibff implementation repositories is not established
family_note: The assigned root README says MACHI consists of separate machife front-end and machibff back-end-for-frontend repositories. Both are public, but neither exposes a root license file or an explicit license grant in its README. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: The root LICENSE history shows a grant-bearing project/metadata commit on 2019-12-20; that does not establish a licensed source year for the essential child repositories. The full source-family grant and any current operational use remain unproven. The root repository last changed in 2021, with no current official product page or deployment mapping found; hold rather than infer that the design description is a maintained software product.

decision_reason: CSI Piemonte's first-party source identifies the MOOn digital-forms product, supplies the complete seven-component source tree and an exact EUPL-1.2-or-later grant, while the current CSI product page documents more than 730 digitized services through March 2025 and names multiple public-sector users. The repository and current product description match on the same end-to-end digital-form and administrative-request workflows; no source/product divergence was found.

government_provenance.note: CSI states that it offers MOOn as its open-source digital-modulistica solution on the Nivola cloud; the CSI repository's README identifies MOOn and carries CSI Piemonte copyright. CSI's governance page documents public member control and its in-house public-administration ICT role: https://www.csipiemonte.it/it/chi-siamo/azienda/governance.

public_source.note: This is CSI's public canonical MOOn repository, with the first-party source directories for citizen and back-office frontends, business-logic services, shared services, printing, and database setup, plus installation guidance for each component.

eligible_license.note: The README declares SPDX EUPL-1.2-or-later and the root LICENSE.txt supplies the EUPL v1.2 grant for first-party source in all seven MOOn components in this monorepo. The README identifies Apache-licensed libraries separately; dependencies and external integrations retain their own grants.

primary_evidence.note: CSI's current product page says more than 730 public-service request workflows were digitized from March 2020 to March 2025 and lists Regione Piemonte, Città Metropolitana di Torino, the regional council, Turin, the University of Turin, and other users. The page describes the same forms, citizen submissions, and back-office case workflow as the repository README, supporting current product/source correspondence and notability.

product_identity: MOOn (Modulistica Open ONline), CSI Piemonte's web platform for configuring/publishing digital forms and managing citizen/business submissions through a back office
agency: CSI Piemonte, the publicly controlled Piedmont ICT consortium/in-house provider; deployments include Regione Piemonte, Città Metropolitana di Torino, Città di Torino, and other entities
license: EUPL-1.2-or-later for the seven first-party MOOn components in the assigned monorepository; Apache and other dependencies/external systems are not included
family_note: The repository contains the citizen front end, citizen business logic, PA back office, back-office business logic, shared services, printing, and database scripts under a root EUPL grant. CSI's current product page identifies MOOn as the same open-source solution and documents ongoing named public-sector use. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: The first public grant-bearing source commit is 2023-09-14 (Initial commit 3.0.0), not a publiccode release date. The repository has been quiet since September 2023, but CSI's current primary page reports 730+ digitized services through March 2025 and names users; its functional description matches the repository's documented platform and component architecture. I found no conflicting current architecture or newer unlinked implementation. This is a maintained-use exception based on current official service evidence plus product-specific source correspondence.

decision_reason: The assigned README documents the distinct regional Notify notification platform and links its implementation components; Regione Piemonte's official technical record states that NOTIFY is deployed in the regional information system, and a 2024 regional product release describes ongoing application-to-Notificatore-to-App-IO workflows. I inspected the full EUPL-1.2 license text in all 11 linked implementation repositories; the core components remain active, with several updated in 2026.

government_provenance.note: Regione Piemonte's official technical-economic record describes NOTIFY as the regional citizen-message notification platform deployed at regional information-system level and documents its role for local public administrations. The CSI first-party root README identifies the platform and component family; CSI's public-member governance is documented at https://www.csipiemonte.it/it/chi-siamo/azienda/governance.

public_source.note: The canonical public project README describes Notify's message broker, preferences, message store, audit/events, email, IO, push, and administrative components and links 11 public first-party source repositories. These repositories form the implementation family, not independent products.

eligible_license.note: The assigned repo and each of the 11 linked implementation repositories contain the full European Union Public Licence v1.2 text (EUPL-1.2): notify-audit, notify-commons, notify-emailconsumer, notify-events, notify-ioconsumer, notify-messagebroker, notify-messagestore, notify-mexconsumer, notify-preferences, notify-pushconsumer, and notify-unpadmin. The grant is scoped to first-party code in each repo; Redis, Firebase, App IO, email/SMS gateways, libraries, and external services keep their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: The Regione Piemonte SIAP/Archivio SIAP release document dated 2024-12-05 describes a batch running every 30 minutes that sends queued procedural notifications to the regional Notificatore for final publication on App IO and lists the initial active workflows. The 2020 regional technical record names that Notificatore as NOTIFY; CSI's current PA-digital page also documents Notify/App IO integration: https://www.csipiemonte.it/it/cosa-facciamo/temi-strategici/trasformazione-digitale. This is a named operational service with live procedural use, not merely a repo listing.

product_identity: Notify (Notificatore Regionale), a regional multi-channel notification platform for public-administration apps, handling preferences, message routing/storage, and email/SMS/push/App IO delivery
agency: CSI Piemonte as developer and regional public-member ICT consortium; Regione Piemonte as operator/sponsor within the regional information system
license: EUPL-1.2 for first-party code in the assigned project repository and each of the 11 linked implementation repositories; external services and dependencies excluded
family_note: The root Notify repository is the product architecture/documentation record; it enumerates 11 code repositories, and I checked each repository's full LICENSE text and found EUPL v1.2. The root was updated 2025-09; components include 2026 activity. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: The root license was public in October 2020 and the earliest licensed first-party implementation component checked (notify-audit) added its EUPL v1.2 grant on 2020-10-16. The Regione Piemonte 2020 record documents the platform in production; its 2024 SIAP release evidence describes the current Notificatore workflow and recurring App IO publication. The exact platform/component descriptions align, and current component repositories show source activity within 2026, so the family passes freshness and source-parity checks.

decision_reason: CSI's current primary pages document Taylor CRM and substantial 2024 use, and the assigned public repository is a Taylor-specific Zammad-derived application. However, the full root license is AGPL version 3 while publiccode.yml declares AGPL-3.0-or-later, leaving the exact grant variant unresolved; the repository has been quiet since January 2023 and no official source-to-current-CRM mapping was found. Hold pending resolution of both gaps.

government_provenance.note: CSI's current primary site identifies Taylor as its Citizen Relationship Management solution designed for public entities and reports it as part of its public-sector services; the assigned repository is hosted and maintained in CSI Piemonte's organization and its README identifies the Taylor-specific service. The CSI governance page documents the consortium's public-member control: https://www.csipiemonte.it/it/chi-siamo/azienda/governance.

public_source.note: The public canonical CSI repository contains Taylor application code, a Taylor-specific README, server requirements and installation instructions. The README states that Taylor is based on the separate open-source Zammad project; this repository is CSI's derivative/application, not a mirror-only record.

eligible_license.note: The actual root LICENSE is the full GNU Affero General Public License version 3 text, which is OSI-approved. However, the repository README describes Zammad as under version 3, while publiccode.yml asserts AGPL-3.0-or-later. Because the exact version grant on CSI-authored source is not consistent across first-party declarations, do not normalize the grant to only or later without rights-holder confirmation. The source's external dependencies retain separate terms.

primary_evidence.note: CSI reports Taylor's 2024 operational metrics (250,000+ tickets, 100,000 users, and €4.6 million saved) and its 2025 annual report describes continued support/evolution of Taylor CRM. But the assigned repo's latest push is 2023-01-13, its README documents an older Zammad-derived stack, and current CSI materials do not link this repository or map its source to the present CRM. Current use is clear; current source correspondence is not.

status_note: The first public grant-bearing initial source commit is 2022-02-21; the 2022-10-10 publiccode releaseDate is not used as the source year. The full LICENSE text and publiccode declaration conflict on the AGPL version option. CSI's 2025 support evidence is current but does not map the quiet 2023 assigned source to the current Taylor CRM service; keep on hold pending direct resolution.

decision_reason: CSI's current 2024 page documents 21 deployed Unlock PA chatbots and substantial monthly interactions, and the public six-component family has exact EUPL-1.2 grants. However, essential component repositories have been quiet since 2021, while the current product is described as an AI-chatbot platform; no official source-to-current-service mapping establishes that this old COVID-era source family still corresponds to today's deployments. Hold for source-parity confirmation.

government_provenance.note: The first-party CSI product page says Unlock PA was developed by CSI in its R&D activity and made available to municipalities; the assigned README credits CSI Piemonte and describes the exact multi-tenant municipal assistant. CSI's public-member governance is documented at https://www.csipiemonte.it/it/chi-siamo/azienda/governance.

public_source.note: The assigned public project README identifies six implementation repositories and provides local Docker-based installation steps. All six linked source repositories are public: unlockpa-db, unlockpa-chatcontrolapi, unlockpa-csibot, unlockpa-unlockbotrasa, unlockpa-backoffice, and unlockpa-examplewebsite.

eligible_license.note: The assigned root repository and each of the six linked implementation repositories contain the full European Union Public Licence v1.2 text (EUPL-1.2). Grants apply per first-party repository; Rasa and other dependencies, trained content/model data, and external integrations remain separately licensed.

primary_evidence.note: CSI's December 2024 primary page identifies Unlock PA as its AI chatbot platform, reports 21 active bots and more than 3,300 monthly contacts, and names current public clients including the Transport Regulatory Authority, Regione Piemonte's car-tax service, and Turin's registry office. Yet the assigned family describes a COVID-era FAQ assistant and its implementation components' latest pushes are from 2021; CSI's current page does not link this source or map it to those bots. Current product use is supported, but current code correspondence is unresolved.

agency: CSI Piemonte, public-member regional ICT consortium and developer; deployments reported for Regione Piemonte, Città di Torino, and the Italian Transport Regulatory Authority

CSI's official December 2024 page proves active use of its product named Unlock PA, but current component code remains quiet since 2021 and the current page does not link or map the assigned source to those deployments. Hold pending an authoritative source-to-current-product link or evidence the source family is still the deployed implementation.
